Corrugated structures exhibit high anisotropic behavior with high stiffness transverse to corrugation and compliance along it.
A corrugated sandwich panel consists of two face sheets and a corrugated core, increasing flexural stiffness by thickening the panel.
Flexural stiffness of a sandwich panel is proportional to the cube of its thickness.
Corrugated sandwich panels have higher shear, bending, and tensile stiffness-to-weight ratios than panels made of only core or face sheet materials.
Corrugated boards are widely used in packaging due to stiffness, lightness, cost-effectiveness, and recyclability.
Corrugated web beams improve buckling stability and reduce weight by about 14% compared to traditional beams.
Corrugated metal sheets are used for roofs and walls in industrial buildings for high strength-to-weight ratio and cost savings.
Corrugated pipes provide strength primarily from geometry rather than wall thickness, enabling lightweight and flexible drainage solutions.
Corrugated sandwich panels are used in marine structures such as decks and bulkheads for weight savings and blast resistance.
Corrugated hoses withstand high pressure, extreme temperatures, and corrosive environments while providing flexibility.
Elastomeric face sheets on corrugated cores provide aerodynamic surfaces without significantly increasing stiffness.
Composite corrugated cores allow optimization of fiber orientation and textile architecture to improve mechanical performance.
Multi-stable corrugated structures can undergo large shape changes and maintain new configurations without locking mechanisms.
Curved corrugated shells enable large elastic shape changes including changes in Gaussian curvature without local stretching.
Hierarchical corrugated cores increase compressive and shear strength by up to ten times compared to first-order cores.
Bi-directional corrugated cores reduce anisotropy and improve transverse shear stiffness by propagating corrugations in two directions.
Pyramidal lattice truss sandwich structures are manufactured by extrusion and electro discharge machining for improved strength-to-weight ratio.
Increasing corrugation curvature radius increases bending stiffness and reduces weight in corrugated web beams.
Corrugated sandwich panels provide multifunctional capabilities including insulation, load-bearing, and thermal protection in aerospace.
Analytical, experimental, and finite element methods are used to study mechanical properties of corrugated panels.
